question: Why is it risky to ignore signs of depression in a patient managing a blood disorder?

options.A: Depression automatically causes an immediate drop in haemoglobin levels
options.B: Patients with depression are legally barred from receiving blood transfusions
options.C: Sadness always leads to permanent physical paralysis if left unmanaged
options.D: Untreated depression can severely reduce treatment adherence and self-care

explanation: When patients feel hopeless, they might skip clinic visits or meds. Spotting depression early keeps them on track with their healing.

question: Why is routine mental health check-in so important when caring for pregnant adolescents?

options.A: Mental health issues only appear in pregnant women under age twenty
options.B: Routine screening replaces the need for blood pressure checks
options.C: Hormonal changes in teens completely erase all risk of anxiety
options.D: Young mothers face high rates of social stigma, isolation, and depression

explanation: Correct! Pregnant teens often face heavy judgment and loneliness, making emotional support and regular check-ins a must.

question: What does 'caregiver burden' mean in community mental health?

options.A: The physical weight of medical equipment kept inside the home
options.B: The physical, emotional, and financial strain experienced by family caregivers
options.C: The mandatory training hours required to become a certified nurse
options.D: The legal responsibility of paying for all hospital admission bills

explanation: You got it! Looking after a loved one with chronic illness at home can take a heavy toll physically and emotionally.

question: Which transport protein moves sodium into the cell while pushing hydrogen ions out in the proximal tubule?

options.A: Bicarbonate chloride exchanger
options.B: Sodium-potassium pump
options.C: Hydrogen ATPase pump
options.D: Sodium-hydrogen exchanger

explanation: Great recall! The sodium-hydrogen exchanger uses the inward rush of sodium to drive hydrogen ions out into the tubule fluid.

question: Why must the secondary piggyback medication bag hang higher than the main IV bag?

options.A: It stops the primary line from ever leaking
options.B: It prevents air bubbles from entering the pump
options.C: Gravity pulls fluid from the higher bag first
options.D: It mixes both medications together instantly

explanation: Physics at work! Hanging the secondary bag higher lets gravity pull that medicine through first before the main bag kicks back in.

question: A patient presents with irregular periods, excess facial hair, and trouble conceiving due to missing ovulation. Which condition does this suggest?

options.A: Normal variant of a short cycle
options.B: Endometriosis of the bowel
options.C: Premature menopause due to surgery
options.D: Polycystic ovary syndrome

explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome is characterized by anovulation, high androgen levels, and irregular menstrual cycles. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h7)

question: When is the best time to introduce palliative care to a cancer patient?

options.A: Early alongside active disease treatment to improve quality of life
options.B: Only when the patient refuses to take prescribed oral medications
options.C: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.D: After all chemotherapy and radiation treatments have failed completely

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the end of life—it teams up with curative treatments from day one to keep the patient comfortable. Excellent holistic nursing!

question: Why is the powerful drug Amphotericin B kept strictly for severe, life-threatening fungal infections?

options.A: It is completely ineffective against superficial mucosal yeast infections
options.B: It must be mixed with specific dietary fats to work properly in the body
options.C: It causes severe allergic reactions in every patient who takes it
options.D: It carries a significant risk of serious organ toxicity, especially to the kidneys

explanation: Amphotericin B is famously strong ("Ampho-terrible" to the kidneys!), so doctors only use it when things are really serious.

question: What is the main goal of conservative management (non-surgical care) for a mild kidney injury?

options.A: Permanently stopping all urine production from both kidneys
options.B: Repairing the kidney capsule immediately via emergency open surgery
options.C: Dissolving internal blood clots with high-dose oral anticoagulants
options.D: Allowing the organ to heal naturally through close monitoring and bed rest

explanation: For minor injuries, the body is amazing at healing itself! Conservative care just means resting and watching the patient closely without rushing into surgery.

question: At what age is primary amenorrhoea typically considered if a young girl has normal breast and pubic hair development but no period yet?

options.A: 18 years
options.B: 11 years
options.C: 15 years
options.D: 21 years

explanation: We look out for primary amenorrhoea if a girl reaches age 15 without starting her period, even though her other puberty signs are normal.

question: What are the classic red flags of a thyrotoxic storm?

options.A: Dangerous high fever and rapid heart rate
options.B: Sudden numbness in the lower legs
options.C: Low body temperature and slow breathing
options.D: Severe dehydration with zero ketones

explanation: Think of a thyrotoxic storm as the body's engine revving completely out of control—leading to high fever, severe tremors, and a racing heart (tachycardia).

question: A patient with hypertension stops taking their drugs because their blood pressure went back to normal. What is this called?

options.A: Erratic adherence
options.B: Creative adjustment
options.C: Premature discontinuation
options.D: Primary non-fulfillment

explanation: Stopping treatment early just because symptoms improve is called premature discontinuation. Remind your patients that the drugs are working *because* they take them!

question: In which part of the female reproductive tract does fertilization usually take place?

options.A: Fallopian tube
options.B: Ovarian cortex
options.C: Uterine cavity
options.D: Cervical canal

explanation: The fallopian tube, specifically the ampulla section, is the normal site where sperm and egg meet and fertilize. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T001#GNS226_U2_T001_h2)

question: The main economic driver for forced marriage in impoverished households is:

options.A: Funding expensive higher education for male siblings
options.B: Gaining immediate access to high-paying government jobs
options.C: Reducing household financial burdens and securing bride wealth
options.D: Paying off international business loans with banks

explanation: Poverty pushes some families to marry off young dependents to cut down expenses and receive financial gains like bride price. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h2)

question: Where should you position the lower edge of the blood pressure cuff on the patient's arm?

options.A: About one inch above the inner elbow crease
options.B: Right up against the shoulder joint
options.C: Directly over the bony wrist
options.D: Halfway down the forearm

explanation: Placing it about an inch above the elbow crease ensures the inner bladder sits right over the brachial artery. Perfect placement!

question: Why is the first few weeks after birth a critical time to watch new mothers closely?

options.A: Severe complications like heavy bleeding and infections happen most often then
options.B: Hormone levels drop to zero immediately after birth
options.C: Babies cry constantly during the first few days
options.D: Mothers are usually discharged before labor pain stops completely

explanation: You've got this! Life-threatening emergencies such as heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) and infections are most common right after delivery, which is why close nursing monitoring is so essential. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h1)

question: In the toxicokinetic process known as ADME, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Mobility
options.B: Mutagenesis
options.C: Metabolism
options.D: Maintenance

explanation: You're doing great! ADME stands for Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion. It simply describes the journey a chemical takes inside the human body.

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to communicate without judgment when assessing these patients?

options.A: It prevents the hospital from paying for laboratory investigations
options.B: It encourages the patient to truthfully share what methods were used, aiding proper treatment
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never experience physical pain
options.D: It is required by criminal law enforcement agencies in all Nigerian states

explanation: When patients feel judged, they hide details like chemical use or instrument trauma. A warm, welcoming attitude saves lives!

question: What should you do if your evaluation shows the patient's care goals were not met?

options.A: Assume the lab equipment is faulty and ignore the recorded results
options.B: Keep the exact same nursing interventions running without changes
options.C: Reassess the situation, identify the barriers, and modify the care plan
options.D: Discharge the patient anyway since the hospital stay has ended

explanation: Nursing is flexible! If a goal isn't met, we figure out what's blocking progress and tweak our care plan to try a new approach.

question: A patient complains of putting on weight fast, being constipated, and feeling cold all the time. Which body system is likely acting up?

options.A: Musculoskeletal system
options.B: Respiratory system
options.C: Urinary system
options.D: Endocrine system

explanation: Correct! These are textbook signs of a sluggish metabolism, which points straight to the endocrine system—specifically an underactive thyroid.

question: How do deficiencies in calcium and vitamin D primarily contribute to fracture risk?

options.A: They increase sudden blood pressure spikes
options.B: They cause muscles to pull too hard on joints
options.C: They stop the bone from forming a blood clot
options.D: They impair proper bone mineralization and strength

explanation: Calcium and vitamin D are essential building blocks for strong bone matrix; without them, bones lose their structural density. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h4)

question: When is the absolute best time for a patient to apply moisturizing creams (emollients)?

options.A: Once a week before going to sleep at night
options.B: Right before taking a hot shower to protect against the hot water
options.C: Only when the skin begins to crack and bleed visibly
options.D: Immediately after bathing while the skin is still slightly damp

explanation: You nailed it! Putting lotion on damp skin traps that wonderful moisture right inside where it belongs.

question: Why would a doctor give a pregnant patient a tocolytic medication?

options.A: To provide effective pain relief during active labour
options.B: To induce rhythmic contractions for a post-dates labour
options.C: To temporarily halt premature uterine contractions
options.D: To prevent heavy bleeding immediately after delivery

explanation: Think of tocolytics as 'time-buys'—they relax the uterus to slow down early labor and give the baby more time to grow.

question: What is the main purpose of adaptive equipment in rehabilitation?

options.A: To help clients perform daily tasks independently despite physical limits
options.B: To monitor the daily vital signs of clients living at home
options.C: To speed up the biological knitting of broken bone fragments
options.D: To completely replace the need for physical therapy and exercise

explanation: Spot on! Adaptive tools give patients clever ways to wash, dress, and eat on their own without always needing help.

question: What happens to a diagnostic skin test if the nurse accidentally injects the medication into the subcutaneous layer?

options.A: The medication crystallizes under the skin and causes infection.
options.B: The patient develops immediate anaphylactic shock.
options.C: The reaction becomes much larger and easier to read.
options.D: The test becomes invalid because the drug absorbs too quickly.

explanation: Subcutaneous tissue has more blood supply, causing rapid absorption that ruins the localized delayed immune reaction needed for a valid test. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h6)

question: A patient cannot wrinkle their forehead or smile evenly on the right side of their face. Which cranial nerve is likely affected?

options.A: Cranial Nerve III
options.B: Cranial Nerve V
options.C: Cranial Nerve VII
options.D: Cranial Nerve XII

explanation: Cranial Nerve VII is the facial nerve! It powers all our facial expressions, so trouble here leads to a drooping or asymmetrical smile.

question: Which blood vessel carries nutrient-rich blood straight from the intestines to the liver?

options.A: Portal vein
options.B: Renal artery
options.C: Inferior vena cava
options.D: Hepatic vein

explanation: You got this! The portal vein acts like a direct highway taking blood filled with digested nutrients straight from your gut to the liver for processing.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to chat about a patient's daily routine before choosing a birth control method?

options.A: To match the patient with a method they can use consistently
options.B: To test the patient's ability to read complex medical textbooks
options.C: To calculate the exact financial tax for purchasing the drugs
options.D: To determine if the patient has any hidden genetic disorders

explanation: Great nursing care is personalized! Knowing a patient's lifestyle helps you suggest a method—like a daily pill versus a 3-year implant—that genuinely fits their everyday life.

question: What is the bed elevation angle for a patient in the semi-Fowler's position?

options.A: Exactly 90 degrees
options.B: 60 to 75 degrees
options.C: 30 to 45 degrees
options.D: 15 to 30 degrees

explanation: Semi-Fowler's raises the head of the bed moderately, usually between 30 and 45 degrees, to aid breathing. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h4)

question: How do patients with neuropathic pain commonly describe what they feel?

options.A: Sharp, localized throbbing after a surgical incision
options.B: Pressure and cramping inside the abdominal cavity
options.C: Burning, shooting, or electric shock sensations
options.D: A dull, constant ache deep inside the bone

explanation: Nerve damage produces characteristic sensory disturbances like burning, tingling, or shooting pains that feel like electricity. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h2)

question: What is your absolute first priority when managing a patient with acute upper airway trauma?

options.A: Giving pain relief medications
options.B: Stopping external bleeding with tight bandages
options.C: Securing and maintaining a clear airway
options.D: Taking a detailed medical history

explanation: Spot on! Airway management always comes first in trauma care to make sure the patient gets enough oxygen before anything else.

question: Where should you put a heavily soiled bed sheet immediately after removing it from the mattress?

options.A: On the clean bedside chair until you finish the bed
options.B: On the clean floor near the foot of the bed temporarily
options.C: Folded neatly on the overbed table for later sorting
options.D: Directly into a designated laundry hamper or bag

explanation: That's right! Putting dirty linen straight into a hamper stops germs from spreading to the floor, furniture, or your uniform.

question: When a patient needs both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, why should the bronchodilator be used first?

options.A: It stops the side effects of the steroid from harming the heart
options.B: It neutralizes stomach acid that might interfere with breathing
options.C: It opens the airways so the steroid can reach deeper into the lungs
options.D: It cleans the mouth so the patient does not develop a fungal infection

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first widens the bronchial tubes, allowing the corticosteroid to penetrate further down into the respiratory tree. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is a primary responsibility of the nurse when initiating a referral?

options.A: Transporting the client personally in her private vehicle
options.B: Performing major surgeries before sending the client away
options.C: Preparing the client emotionally and explaining the reason for referral
options.D: Purchasing the client's transport fare out of her own pocket

explanation: Nurses must counsel clients so they understand why a referral is necessary and feel less anxious about visiting a new facility. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h6)

question: Which of these does NOT help cause a disease outbreak?

options.A: High routine immunization coverage in children
options.B: Inadequate waste management systems
options.C: Poor access to safe, clean drinking water
options.D: Overcrowded housing and living quarters

explanation: Vaccines are our shield! High immunization rates protect a community and stop outbreaks, unlike bad water or crowded living spaces which spread disease.

question: What is a major risk of very high fevers, especially in young children?

options.A: Weak bones
options.B: Low blood cholesterol
options.C: Vision loss
options.D: Febrile seizures

explanation: Correct! When a child's temperature shoots up too fast, it can sometimes trigger a febrile seizure.

question: A patient was just extubated 20 minutes ago and now has a high-pitched whistling sound when breathing in. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Immediate accumulation of secretions in the left main bronchus
options.B: Sudden tension pneumothorax from previous positive pressure
options.C: Anxiety-induced hyperventilation following tube removal
options.D: Laryngeal edema causing partial upper airway obstruction

explanation: That high-pitched sound (stridor) usually means the voice box (larynx) got a little swollen and angry from having the breathing tube resting in it. Good catch!

question: What is the main duty of the anaesthetist during an operation?

options.A: Monitoring the patient's vital signs and managing pain
options.B: Transporting the patient safely from the ward to theatre
options.C: Documenting sponge and instrument counts every thirty minutes
options.D: Handing sterile instruments directly to the operating surgeon

explanation: The anaesthetist focuses entirely on keeping the patient asleep, stable, and pain-free while watching all life signs closely. They are the patient's guardian angels for comfort!

question: Why must a nurse always get explicit consent before referring a survivor to another agency?

options.A: To protect the survivor's safety and maintain strict confidentiality
options.B: To ensure the outside agency has enough physical medicine in stock
options.C: To test whether the patient understands basic medical terminology
options.D: To comply with hospital billing and insurance reimbursement rules

explanation: Sharing a survivor's personal details without their permission can put them in serious physical danger and break ethical rules.

question: Which surgical method allows a doctor to remove a uterine septum without making any cuts on the skin?

options.A: Abdominal laparotomy
options.B: Hysteroscopy
options.C: Vaginal colporrhaphy
options.D: Total hysterectomy

explanation: Brilliant! Hysteroscopy lets the surgeon work right inside the womb by passing tiny instruments through the vagina and cervix—no abdominal cuts needed!

question: During the final stage of bone healing, what is the main job of osteoclasts?

options.A: Forming the initial blood clot within the broken bone ends
options.B: Producing new collagen fibers to strengthen the soft callus
options.C: Resorbing excess bone tissue to restore the original bone shape
options.D: Laying down a soft cartilage bridge across the fracture gap

explanation: Think of osteoclasts as the body's sculptors. They clear away any extra, messy bone tissue laid down during healing to smooth the bone back to its normal shape. You're doing great!

question: Which specific immune cells does HIV attack and destroy?

options.A: CD4 cells
options.B: Red blood cells
options.C: Platelets
options.D: Neutrophils

explanation: Spot on! HIV targets CD4 helper T-cells, which gradually weakens the body's immune defenses. You've got this!

question: How does a receptor antagonist antidote work to reverse an overdose?

options.A: It binds to heavy metals and flushes them out through the urine
options.B: It attaches to the same cell sites as the poison to block its action
options.C: It coats the lining of the stomach so the poison cannot pass through
options.D: It destroys the chemical structure of the poison inside the blood

explanation: Think of it like musical chairs! The antagonist rushes in and sits on the cell receptors first, blocking the poison from grabbing a seat and doing damage.

question: A nurse is getting blood tubes ready to send to a lab across town. What should she do first?

options.A: Attach a 24-hour emergency contact phone number directly onto the patient's arm
options.B: Drop the loose glass tubes directly into a standard red plastic hospital waste bag
options.C: Verify that tube caps are tightly sealed and place them into an approved secondary container
options.D: Wrap the unsecured tubes in paper towels and place them in an ordinary cardboard shoe box

explanation: Safety first! Always check that caps are secure and use the proper secondary container before moving samples off-site.

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for at the very beginning of the SBAR communication tool?

options.A: Solution
options.B: Situation
options.C: Severity
options.D: Symptoms

explanation: Spot on! In SBAR, the first 'S' is for Situation—a quick summary of what is happening right now that made you call or report.

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand normal female anatomy and physiology?

options.A: To diagnose rare genetic abnormalities routinely
options.B: To tell healthy development apart from actual illness
options.C: To prevent natural menopause from happening
options.D: To prescribe hormone therapy for every patient

explanation: Spotting what's normal is your superpower as a nurse! Once you know what a healthy cycle or transition looks like, you can easily catch when something needs medical attention.

question: What marks the transition period of adolescence?

options.A: Fixed behavioral patterns
options.B: The cessation of brain development
options.C: Complete emotional and financial independence
options.D: Rapid physical, emotional, and social changes

explanation: Adolescence is defined as a transitional phase marked by rapid changes across physical, emotional, and social domains. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h1)

question: What is the main reason for using aseptic technique during surgery?

options.A: To reduce the cost of surgical supplies
options.B: To make the surgical room smell clean
options.C: To eliminate all micro-organisms from the surgical field
options.D: To speed up the recovery time after anesthesia

explanation: Great job! Aseptic technique blocks germs and bad bugs from getting into the patient's vulnerable body tissues.

question: Why do judgmental attitudes from healthcare workers act as a barrier to family planning?

options.A: Clients will demand more expensive medications than needed
options.B: Clients will avoid seeking care out of fear of being shamed or scolded
options.C: The clinic electricity will shut down due to negative energy
options.D: Staff members will forget how to write medical prescriptions

explanation: When providers judge clients for their choices, age, or marital status, patients stop coming to the clinic, leading to unmet health needs. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h6)

question: What kind of drug property makes it most likely to build up in breast milk for the baby to absorb?

options.A: A long half-life combined with high lipid solubility
options.B: High protein binding capacity in maternal blood
options.C: Water solubility with a very long elimination time
options.D: Complete destruction by the maternal stomach acid

explanation: Drugs that dissolve easily in fat (lipid-soluble) and hang around in the body a long time (long half-life) tend to linger in breast milk.

question: Why do patients with long-term atrial fibrillation often take blood thinners (anticoagulants)?

options.A: To strengthen the squeezing force of the left and right ventricular muscles
options.B: To slow down the electrical conduction speed through the atrioventricular node
options.C: To prevent blood clots from forming in the quivering atria and traveling to the brain
options.D: To lower systemic blood pressure and reduce strain on the coronary arteries

explanation: When the atria quiver instead of squeezing properly, blood sits still and can form clots. Blood thinners stop these clots from forming and traveling up to cause a stroke. Great clinical reasoning!

question: Which blood-borne infection has the highest statistical risk of transmission after a single accidental needle-stick?

options.A: Hepatitis C virus
options.B: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.C: Hepatitis B virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Hepatitis B is remarkably hardy and infectious. That is why getting your Hep B vaccine and safety training early in nursing school is so important!

question: A nursing mother complains of sharp nipple pain and visible cracks. What should you as a nurse check first?

options.A: Suggest weaning the baby to formula immediately
options.B: Recommend applying strong antiseptic ointments before every feed
options.C: Assess the infant's latch technique and mouth positioning during feeding
options.D: Advise the mother to stop breastfeeding completely for one week

explanation: Fixing how the baby takes the breast stops further damage and lets the skin heal naturally. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: What major upper reproductive tract condition can happen if cervicitis is left untreated?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Endometriosis of the bowel
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)

explanation: If lower tract infections aren't cleared, they can creep upward and turn into pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

question: What is reported as the most common barrier to HIV disclosure?

options.A: Forgetting one's own diagnosis date
options.B: Lack of available transportation to the clinic
options.C: Excessive availability of antiretroviral drugs
options.D: Fear of stigma and discrimination

explanation: Societal prejudice and harsh judgment make people terrified of how others will treat them after learning their status. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h5)

question: A young woman comes to the clinic with sudden, severe pain on one side of her lower abdomen and vomiting. What condition should the nurse think of first?

options.A: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.B: Follicular cyst rupture
options.C: Ovarian torsion
options.D: Endometriosis flare-up

explanation: Sudden one-sided pain and vomiting are classic red flags for ovarian torsion, where the ovary twists and cuts off its own blood supply. It's a true emergency!

question: Why does functional decline in degenerative disorders often fluctuate day-to-day?

options.A: Immune systems fight off the genetic code
options.B: Therapists alter medications every morning
options.C: Genetic mutations change their sequence daily
options.D: Patients experience varying levels of fatigue and stiffness

explanation: Factors like exhaustion, muscle stiffness, and small changes in health can cause daily ups and downs in what a patient is able to do. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h2)

question: Which test is primarily used to check the electrical activity of the brain?

options.A: Echocardiogram
options.B: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.C: Electroencephalogram (EEG)
options.D: Electromyogram (EMG)

explanation: Correct! An EEG records brain waves and helps doctors spot abnormal electrical patterns.

question: Why must nurses learn about different cultural and spiritual beliefs surrounding death?

options.A: To determine how much money the family can spend on a funeral
options.B: To prove which religion handles grief better than others
options.C: To ensure every family follows the exact same hospital protocol
options.D: To respect diverse mourning practices and avoid imposing personal biases

explanation: Cultural safety means honoring traditions and spiritual needs without letting personal judgments get in the way of great care.

question: Why do intramuscular injections get absorbed faster than subcutaneous ones?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat contains no blood vessels
options.B: Muscles produce enzymes that break down drugs
options.C: The needle used is always much thinner
options.D: Muscle tissue has a rich blood supply

explanation: Great job thinking about how drugs move in the body! Muscles have plenty of blood vessels, which helps medications rush quickly into the bloodstream. You've got this!

question: What is the most important first step when a patient rings the bell asking for nausea medication?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of cold water
options.B: Immediately administer a broad-spectrum 5-HT3 antagonist IV
options.C: Assess the character, frequency, and potential triggers of the nausea
options.D: Insert a nasogastric tube to decompress the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Always assess first before giving meds. Understanding what's causing the nausea helps you pick the right treatment and catch hidden dangers. Excellent nursing judgment!

question: Why must nurses monitor vital signs very closely when a patient is going through alcohol withdrawal?

options.A: It ensures the patient stays awake during visiting hours
options.B: It helps the patient lose weight faster during hospitalization
options.C: Severe withdrawal can cause dangerous spikes in blood pressure and seizures
options.D: It is required to calculate the exact hospital bill total

explanation: Alcohol withdrawal can be very dangerous, triggering severe tremors, high blood pressure, and seizures. Careful monitoring saves lives!

question: How does a fear of blame usually affect a nurse's problem-solving ability?

options.A: It improves the nurse's analytical and critical thinking skills
options.B: It encourages the nurse to report errors immediately
options.C: It causes the nurse to hide mistakes instead of fixing them
options.D: It helps the healthcare team work faster during emergencies

explanation: When people fear punishment, they tend to conceal errors rather than addressing the root problem openly. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which medication class is appropriate for a patient experiencing severe pain at Step 3 of the WHO analgesic ladder?

options.A: Strong opioids such as morphine
options.B: Skeletal muscle relaxants alone
options.C: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.D: Mild opioids such as codeine

explanation: Step 3 of the WHO ladder is designed for severe pain and utilizes strong opioids like morphine, fentanyl, or oxycodone. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h4)

question: Why is an erection that lasts over four hours (priapism) a medical emergency?

options.A: It results in permanent loss of bladder control
options.B: It triggers rapid systemic hypertension
options.C: It causes immediate rupture of the urethra
options.D: It leads to permanent damage from trapped, oxygen-depleted blood

explanation: When blood gets stuck without fresh circulation coming in, the tissues are starved of oxygen and can suffer permanent damage very quickly. Fast action is key!

question: What is a major consequence of missing feedback letters from the receiving facility?

options.A: The client automatically becomes pregnant within one week
options.B: The primary clinic is forced to close down permanently
options.C: The primary nurse remains unaware of whether the client received care
options.D: The nurse receives a financial bonus from the government

explanation: Without feedback loops, primary nurses cannot track client outcomes or ensure continuity of community-level care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h7)

question: Which two mental health conditions are most commonly diagnosed in people living with HIV?

options.A: Schizophrenia and bipolar disorder
options.B: Obsessive-compulsive disorder and phobias
options.C: Anorexia nervosa and bulimia
options.D: Depression and anxiety

explanation: Dealing with a chronic illness and facing social judgment can understandably take a toll, often leading to depression and anxiety.

question: Why do many hyperthyroid patients in low-resource settings often arrive at the hospital with very advanced illness?

options.A: Delays in reaching specialized care and initial use of traditional remedies
options.B: Widespread mandatory fortification of local staple foods with thyroxine
options.C: Genetic mutations that make local strains of the disease grow faster
options.D: Strict government bans on importing standard antithyroid medicines

explanation: Long distances to health facilities and trying local herbal remedies first often mean patients only reach the hospital when their illness is quite advanced.

question: In which part of the abdomen is the main portion of the stomach located?

options.A: Lower left quadrant
options.B: Upper left quadrant
options.C: Upper right quadrant
options.D: Lower right quadrant

explanation: Think of the abdomen in four quarters. The stomach rests comfortably right up in the upper left section, just below your diaphragm.

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse should do?

options.A: Ignoring community input to enforce rapid medical compliance
options.B: Advocating for fair resource distribution among marginalized groups
options.C: Respecting cultural traditions while promoting health education
options.D: Protecting patient confidentiality during home visits

explanation: Correct! Community nursing is all about teamwork and partnership—we never force things, but rather work together with the people we care for.

question: What is the primary benefit of getting a COVID-19 vaccine?

options.A: Reducing the risk of severe illness and hospitalization
options.B: Curing existing long-term respiratory complications
options.C: Guaranteeing that a person will never catch the virus
options.D: Eliminating the need for hand hygiene and masks

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines train your immune system to fight off the worst parts of the disease, keeping you out of the hospital.

question: Why is drug under-prescription often a hidden problem in healthcare?

options.A: Pharmacies automatically correct the missing prescriptions
options.B: It is completely illegal and hidden by hospital administrators
options.C: Patients refuse to report when their doctor forgets a drug
options.D: It involves omissions of care rather than active errors that cause immediate toxicity

explanation: Great job thinking about patient safety! When something is left out (an omission), it doesn't cause a sudden toxic reaction, making it much harder to spot right away compared to an overdose.

question: What is the big difference between bactericidal and bacteriostatic drugs?

options.A: Bactericidal agents require acidic pH, while bacteriostatic agents need alkaline pH
options.B: Bacteriostatic drugs work only in the lungs, while bactericidal drugs work everywhere
options.C: Bactericidal drugs kill bacteria, whereas bacteriostatic drugs stop their growth
options.D: Bacteriostatic drugs destroy human cells, but bactericidal drugs protect them

explanation: Easy to remember: Bacterici-DAL drugs outright KILL the bacteria, while bacteriostatic drugs just press 'pause' on their growth and let your immune system finish the job!

question: A patient is diagnosed with a tumor growing in the smooth muscle of the thigh. Which classification applies best?

options.A: Sarcoma
options.B: Carcinoma
options.C: Lymphoma
options.D: Leukemia

explanation: Connective and supportive tissues like muscle, bone, and fat give rise to sarcomas rather than carcinomas. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why might a cancer care plan shift from trying to cure the disease to focusing purely on comfort and palliation?

options.A: Standard surgical options are suddenly much safer than outpatient chemotherapy.
options.B: The patient's insurance policy has expired and can no longer cover active medications.
options.C: The nursing staff prefers managing comfort care over administering toxic drugs.
options.D: The disease has progressed beyond the point where a cure or control is realistically achievable.

explanation: Spot on! When the disease advances past where treatment can stop it, the healthcare team shifts gears to palliation—focusing entirely on comfort, symptom relief, and quality of life.

question: Why do doctors often order bladder irrigation right after prostate surgery?

options.A: To stretch the bladder muscle back to its normal size
options.B: To prevent dangerous blood clots from blocking urine drainage
options.C: To deliver strong pain medication directly into the bloodstream
options.D: To check if the kidneys are producing enough red blood cells

explanation: Spot on! Surgery areas tend to bleed a bit, and a steady flush stops clots from choking off the catheter.

question: What is the main job of desmosomes in heart muscle cells?

options.A: Isolating the atria electrically from the lower ventricles
options.B: Holding adjacent muscle cells tightly together during strong contractions
options.C: Producing adenosine triphosphate for resting heart muscle
options.D: Regulating the flow of calcium ions into the cell interior

explanation: Desmosomes act like heavy-duty rivets. When the heart squeezes hard, they keep the cells from pulling apart!

question: A patient has a deep, suspicious mole that needs to be completely removed with a clear border of healthy skin. Which method is best?

options.A: Shave biopsy
options.B: Punch biopsy core
options.C: Excisional biopsy
options.D: Superficial scraping

explanation: An excisional biopsy takes out the entire lesion plus a small safety margin of healthy skin around it—great when we need total removal, like checking for melanoma.

question: A patient collapses in the hospital hallway. What is the maximum time a nurse should spend checking for normal breathing?

options.A: 30 seconds
options.B: 1 minute
options.C: 2 minutes
options.D: 10 seconds

explanation: Keep it quick! Spend no more than 10 seconds checking for breathing so you don't delay starting chest compressions.

question: What is the name of the natural pacemaker that sets the rhythm for the heart?

options.A: Purkinje fiber
options.B: Bundle of His
options.C: Atrioventricular node
options.D: Sinoatrial node

explanation: The Sinoatrial (SA) node is the boss of heart rhythms! It fires off electrical signals the fastest, keeping the whole heart beating in a steady, regular pattern.

question: What main process causes tissue damage inside the pancreas during acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Infection of pancreatic tissue by gut bacteria traveling upward
options.B: Rapid formation of scar tissue blocking the pancreatic duct
options.C: Autodigestion of the pancreas by its own early-activated enzymes
options.D: Complete lack of blood supply caused by sudden heart failure

explanation: Think of it as friendly fire! Digestive enzymes turn on too early while still inside the pancreas, and they accidentally start breaking down the organ's own tissue.

question: Why do doctors most commonly perform a colostomy?

options.A: To permanently cure long-term constipation without changing diet
options.B: To bypass or remove a diseased or damaged part of the bowel
options.C: To allow direct medicine administration into the bloodstream
options.D: To increase the length of the small intestine for better food absorption

explanation: Spot on! Conditions like severe infection, injury, or cancer mean we need to safely divert waste away from a sick section of the large intestine.

question: What are the two major parts that make up the human nervous system?

options.A: Spinal cord and vertebral column
options.B: Sympathetic and parasympathetic systems
options.C: Central and peripheral nervous systems
options.D: Brain and cranial nerves

explanation: Spot on! The nervous system splits into two main teams: the central nervous system (your brain and spinal cord) and the peripheral nervous system (all the nerves branching out to the rest of your body).

question: Which of the following is NOT a core component of a standard cardiac rehabilitation program?

options.A: Nutritional counseling and diet advice
options.B: High-dose intravenous chemotherapy
options.C: Supervised physical exercise training
options.D: Education on quitting cigarette smoking

explanation: Chemotherapy treats cancer, not coronary artery disease; cardiac rehab focuses on exercise, nutrition, and lifestyle changes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h9)

question: What is the maximum recommended time for a single suction pass?

options.A: 3 to 5 minutes
options.B: 1 to 2 minutes
options.C: 30 to 45 seconds
options.D: 10 to 15 seconds

explanation: Limiting passes to 10 to 15 seconds prevents the patient from running out of oxygen and developing dangerous heart rhythms. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h5)

question: Why is keeping an eye on chronic health conditions so important during post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees immediate fertility restoration
options.B: It prevents minor issues from becoming emergencies
options.C: It eliminates the need for pain medication
options.D: It reduces hospital administrative costs

explanation: Spotting and managing chronic diseases early stops them from flaring up and getting worse during a time when the body is under physical stress.

question: Why must calcium bind to troponin before a muscle can contract?

options.A: It directly provides the energy needed for the power stroke
options.B: It moves tropomyosin away from actin binding sites
options.C: It holds the Z-lines firmly in place during movement
options.D: It destroys excess acetylcholine in the synapse

explanation: At rest, tropomyosin blocks the binding sites like a locked door. Calcium acts as the key that shifts it out of the way so the muscle can get to work! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why is it important to talk calmly with a nervous patient during an MRI scan?

options.A: To test if their cranial nerves are working
options.B: To distract them so they fall fast asleep
options.C: To keep their blood pressure high during the test
options.D: To reassure them and help them stay still so pictures aren't blurred

explanation: MRI machines are loud and tight spaces. A reassuring voice helps patients stay still so the images turn out clear.

question: A nurse is getting the tray ready for a sigmoidoscopy. Which tool is needed if the doctor wants to take a sample of a suspicious spot?

options.A: An IV infusion pump
options.B: A urinary catheter
options.C: A rigid speculum
options.D: Biopsy forceps

explanation: Awesome! Biopsy forceps slide right through the scope to pinch a tiny, painless tissue sample for the lab to check.

question: What special tools do cancer cells use to break through surrounding tissue barriers?

options.A: Matrix metalloproteinases
options.B: Gastric digestive pepsins
options.C: Liver clotting factors
options.D: Insulin receptor enzymes

explanation: MMPs act like little scissors or chemical drills, helping cancer cells chew through the matrix and invade surrounding tissue.

question: A 16-year-old girl visits your clinic for family planning advice but is terrified her parents will find out. How should you respond as a nurse?

options.A: Scold her for engaging in premarital relationships
options.B: Refuse service and call her parents immediately
options.C: Assure her of confidentiality and provide age-appropriate counseling
options.D: Report her to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Trust is everything in nursing! By assuring her of confidentiality, you make her feel safe enough to get the right health education and protection instead of hiding risky situations.

question: When a nurse gently pinches the skin to check hydration (skin turgor), which fibers in the dermis make the skin snap back?

options.A: Sebum and sweat secretions
options.B: Collagen and elastin fibers
options.C: Melanin and keratin proteins
options.D: Adipose and nervous tissues

explanation: Brilliant! Collagen and elastin give the dermis its spring and flexibility, helping nurses quickly check if a patient is well-hydrated.

question: As a smart nurse, which lab result must you check before a patient has a thoracentesis?

options.A: Blood glucose levels
options.B: Liver enzyme markers
options.C: Coagulation profiles
options.D: Thyroid hormone panel

explanation: Brilliant! Always check clotting times and platelets first so you know the patient won't run into any heavy bleeding issues during the procedure.

question: What key lifestyle advice should a nurse include when educating a patient with prediabetes?

options.A: Avoid all types of physical movement to preserve energy
options.B: Sleep for at least fourteen hours every single night
options.C: Incorporate a balanced diet and regular physical activity
options.D: Eliminate all forms of water from the daily diet

explanation: Dietary changes and regular exercise help improve insulin sensitivity and prevent prediabetes from advancing to full diabetes. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h9)

question: What happens when a normal proto-oncogene gets mutated?

options.A: It turns into an oncogene that drives nonstop cell division
options.B: It immediately forces the cell to undergo programmed death
options.C: It repairs all surrounding damaged DNA strands instantly
options.D: It stops all cellular activity and puts the cell to sleep

explanation: Proto-oncogenes are like the gas pedal for cell growth. When mutated, they become oncogenes that push the pedal all the way down!

question: Which blood test is the most specific indicator of heart muscle damage during a heart attack?

options.A: Complete blood count
options.B: Liver function enzymes
options.C: Serum electrolytes
options.D: Cardiac troponin

explanation: Troponin proteins are released directly into the bloodstream when heart muscle cells are injured or die, making it the primary marker for a heart attack. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h5)

question: What unit of measurement is commonly used to express energy expenditure in human nutrition?

options.A: Centimeters
options.B: Kilocalories
options.C: Milligrams
options.D: Milliliters

explanation: Energy in human nutrition is measured in kilocalories, which people commonly call calories. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h1)

question: Which type of ovarian cyst can contain unusual tissues like hair or teeth?

options.A: Follicular cyst
options.B: Dermoid cyst
options.C: Endometrioma
options.D: Corpus luteum cyst

explanation: Dermoid cysts sound a bit wild, but they just develop from germ cells and can sometimes contain quirky tissues like skin, hair, or teeth!

question: What activity rule should you teach a patient before they go home after a liver biopsy?

options.A: Eat no solid foods for the next five days
options.B: Avoid heavy lifting and hard exercise for at least a week
options.C: Stay in bed in a dark room for two whole weeks
options.D: Keep your right arm strapped in a sling for two days

explanation: Spot on! Straining or lifting increases pressure inside the belly, which can trigger bleeding even days later. Rest is key!

question: Why is tele-nursing particularly helpful for patients living in remote areas?

options.A: It brings healthcare services directly to homes without requiring travel
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never need hospital admission
options.C: It provides free medications delivered straight to the doorstep
options.D: It completely replaces the need for any physical doctor visits

explanation: By using technology, nurses can assess and monitor clients who live far away from physical health facilities. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why is prevention so important in cancer care?

options.A: It replaces the need for surgical removal of tumors in every single patient.
options.B: It completely eliminates the requirement for diagnostic lab testing.
options.C: It stops the disease early, reducing suffering and healthcare costs.
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never experience any genetic mutations in their lifetime.

explanation: Preventing cancer or catching it early spares your future patients from aggressive treatments and helps them live longer, healthier lives.

question: A patient states they have smoked for twenty years and wonders if quitting will even help now. What is the most accurate nursing response?

options.A: Smoking only affects your lungs, not your heart or blood vessels
options.B: You must stop all at once without any help or replacement products for it to work
options.C: Quitting will benefit your heart immediately, cutting your heart disease risk in half within one year
options.D: The damage is already permanent, so quitting will not change your risk level

explanation: Cardiovascular benefits begin almost immediately after quitting smoking, and within twelve months, the excess risk of coronary heart disease drops by fifty percent. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h5)

question: What is a major cause of fear for patients admitted to the hospital?

options.A: Eating meals at standard hospital times
options.B: Loss of personal autonomy and daily control
options.C: Having too many visitors during the day
options.D: Choosing their own room temperature

explanation: Spot on! Having to hand over control of your daily routine and independence to hospital staff can feel really scary and overwhelming.

question: What is the main difference between physical dependence on a drug and psychological addiction?

options.A: Addiction stops the moment you lower the dose
options.B: Dependence only happens to people who abuse drugs
options.C: Dependence is a normal body adaptation, while addiction involves strong cravings
options.D: Dependence stops future pain relief from working

explanation: Physical dependence just means your body gets used to a medicine and reacts if you stop too fast. Addiction is a brain disease marked by compulsive cravings and loss of control.

question: How does palliative care view the dying process?

options.A: As an emergency requiring immediate surgery
options.B: As a normal part of the human life cycle
options.C: As a medical failure that must be avoided
options.D: As a punishment for past life actions

explanation: Palliative care respects life's natural journey. It doesn't rush death, nor does it try to unnaturally drag it out—it accepts it as a normal part of living.

question: What is the common name for the suspensory ligaments that support the breast?

options.A: Pectoral tendons
options.B: Inguinal fibers
options.C: Fallopian bands
options.D: Cooper's ligaments

explanation: Cooper's ligaments are fibrous bands that connect the chest wall fascia to the skin, holding the breast upright. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h5)

question: What is anticipatory grief?

options.A: Anger directed at doctors after a misdiagnosis
options.B: Depression caused by a sudden physical injury
options.C: Grief experienced before the actual death occurs
options.D: Relief felt when a patient finally passes away

explanation: Anticipatory grief is the mourning process that happens prior to an expected death as losses accumulate. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h6)

question: What is another name for the Pouch of Douglas in female anatomy?

options.A: Rectouterine pouch
options.B: Broad ligament recess
options.C: Vesicouterine pouch
options.D: Parametrial space

explanation: You've got this! We call it the rectouterine pouch because it sits right between the rectum and the uterus. Simple and straightforward!

question: When is a statistical table best used in a research report?

options.A: When replacing the narrative text entirely
options.B: When describing a single patient's emotional journey
options.C: When presenting large amounts of precise numerical data
options.D: When showing general trends and patterns over time

explanation: Tables excel at organizing large volumes of exact numbers so readers can easily locate specific values. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced in community health planning in Nigeria?

options.A: Cultural resistance and rumors regarding certain public health programs
options.B: Excessive availability of surplus financial funds in primary health centers
options.C: Poor transportation infrastructure in remote rural or riverine areas
options.D: Inadequate funding and delayed budgetary releases from government

explanation: Primary health centers in Nigeria typically suffer from chronic underfunding rather than having excessive surplus funds. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)

question: Which mineral is especially important for growing and building white blood cells to fight infections?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Zinc
options.D: Sodium

explanation: You got it! Zinc plays a huge role in helping your immune cells multiply and do their job when an infection tries to take hold.

question: What is the very first step when solving a problem?

options.A: Identifying and clearly defining the problem
options.B: Implementing a quick temporary fix immediately
options.C: Writing a formal report for the hospital board
options.D: Blaming the staff member who made the error

explanation: You can't fix an issue until you truly understand what is going wrong. Pinpoint the real problem first!

question: Why does the WHO stress having a steady supply of injection equipment?

options.A: Having extra supplies makes nurses finish their shifts much faster
options.B: Patients refuse treatment if clinics do not show them brand new boxes
options.C: Shortages often force workers to reuse single-use devices out of desperation
options.D: Government regulations require clinics to store at least ten years of stock

explanation: When clinics run out of disposables, it puts immense pressure on nurses. Reliable supplies keep everyone safe from risky workarounds.

question: A nurse is changing a dressing on a large surgical abdominal wound. What is the primary reason for using sterile instruments and supplies?

options.A: To make the dressing change process faster and easier
options.B: To prevent bacteria from entering the open surgical wound
options.C: To stop the patient from feeling pain during the procedure
options.D: To remove old scar tissue from previous operations

explanation: Open wounds are direct pathways for bacteria to cause local infection or systemic sepsis, making sterile tools essential. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h7)

question: What does a Doppler ultrasound check in a vascular patient?

options.A: Blood electrolyte and kidney filtration levels
options.B: Blood flow speed and whether vessels are open
options.C: Electrical heart rhythms
options.D: Bone strength and joint health

explanation: A Doppler ultrasound uses harmless sound waves to 'listen' to blood moving through vessels, helping us see if there are blockages or if blood is flowing backward.

question: How do patient satisfaction surveys and attendance logs help an adolescent health clinic?

options.A: They prove to the government that no teenagers are sick in the area
options.B: They guarantee that the clinic will receive international funding
options.C: They allow the team to identify gaps and improve services over time
options.D: They replace the need for physical examinations during consultations

explanation: Tracking data and feedback helps clinics see what is working well and where changes are needed to better serve youths. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h8)

question: What is the most common immediate complication to watch for after a male circumcision?

options.A: Hemorrhage
options.B: Total urinary retention
options.C: Erectile dysfunction
options.D: Meatal stenosis

explanation: Because the male genital area has a rich blood supply, bleeding (hemorrhage) is the most frequent acute thing to monitor for right after the procedure.

question: When changing sheets for a bedridden patient who cannot get up, how should you handle the top covers?

options.A: Place the clean top sheet over the old one, then pull the old sheet out from underneath
options.B: Ask the patient to hold the dirty blanket up with both hands
options.C: Remove all covers completely, leaving the patient uncovered until the end
options.D: Strip the top of the bed first and replace sheets while the patient sits up

explanation: Spot on! Layering the clean cover over the old one before sliding the old one out keeps your patient warm and protects their privacy the whole time.

question: Which baby health problems are most common when born to teenage mothers?

options.A: Congenital heart murmurs caused by maternal stress
options.B: Advanced bone maturation at birth
options.C: Premature birth and low birth weight
options.D: Excessive birth weight and overgrown organs

explanation: Spot on! Because the mother's body is still growing, babies often arrive too early and small.

question: Which lab test is the most reliable way to track declining kidney function?

options.A: Platelet aggregation rate
options.B: White blood cell count
options.C: Serum sodium concentration
options.D: Glomerular filtration rate

explanation: The GFR (Glomerular Filtration Rate) tells us directly how well the kidneys are cleaning the blood, making it the gold standard for checking kidney health.

question: Why does the body rely on both innate and adaptive defenses?

options.A: Innate destroys viruses while adaptive only handles bacterial infections
options.B: Innate immunity creates antibodies while adaptive creates physical barriers
options.C: Adaptive defense works entirely independently of the innate system
options.D: Innate provides immediate defense while adaptive targets specific invaders later

explanation: Spot on! Innate immunity jumps in instantly to buy time, while the adaptive system gears up to launch a precise, targeted attack.

question: Which of these procedures is typically done in a casualty or minor theatre?

options.A: Removing a brain tumor
options.B: Performing an open heart valve replacement
options.C: Suturing a deep facial laceration
options.D: Doing a total hip arthroplasty

explanation: Correct! Minor procedures like stitching up cuts fit perfectly in the casualty theatre, freeing up the big ORs for massive surgeries.

question: Which client is most at risk for having a very hard time adjusting after losing a spouse?

options.A: A client who anticipated the death for many years following a chronic illness
options.B: A client with limited social support who depended entirely on the spouse for daily functioning
options.C: A client who participates actively in a supportive religious community
options.D: A client who has successfully coped with multiple past life crises

explanation: Spot on! When someone relies completely on their partner and lacks a strong backup support system, the loss hits much harder and recovery is tougher.

question: After a very tough shift, which activity helps a nurse process their emotions and learn from the experience?

options.A: Ignoring the incident
options.B: Reflective journaling
options.C: Changing clinical wards
options.D: Filing an incident report

explanation: Writing down your thoughts in a reflective journal is a great way to unwind, process tough moments, and grow into a stronger nurse.

question: What main change happens inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli) during pneumonia?

options.A: The walls permanently stretch and lose stretchiness.
options.B: Blood flow to the lungs completely stops overnight.
options.C: Fluid, pus, and cellular debris fill up the spaces.
options.D: The breathing tubes stretch out and trap air.

explanation: As the body fights the infection, fluid and white blood cells flood the alveoli. That's why air has such a hard time getting in!

question: Why is counting needles such an important duty for a nurse?

options.A: It speeds up the surgeon's work during complex procedures
options.B: It serves as a legal and physical safety barrier for the patient
options.C: It is only done to satisfy hospital administrative rules
options.D: It reduces the need to sterilize instruments after the case

explanation: Great job thinking about patient safety! Accurate counts protect your patient from harm and protect you and your team legally. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why are injections uniquely risky when it comes to spreading diseases?

options.A: It increases the normal body temperature of the recipient
options.B: It destroys all white blood cells found near the injection site
options.C: It forces medications to travel too quickly through the digestive tract
options.D: It bypasses the skin, creating a direct pathway into the body's tissues

explanation: Our skin is an amazing shield against germs. A needle breaks that shield, making injections a super-highway straight into the body if we aren't careful.

question: Why is there fluid between the thin membranes that wrap around our organs?

options.A: To transmit nerve signals to the brain
options.B: To digest food particles in the stomach
options.C: To carry oxygen through the bloodstream
options.D: To reduce friction during organ movement

explanation: Imagine two sliding doors with oil between them. This fluid lubricates the membranes so your heart and lungs can glide smoothly without rubbing raw!

question: Which global body defines nursing as autonomous and collaborative care for people of all ages in all settings?

options.A: West African Health Organization
options.B: International Council of Nurses
options.C: Red Cross International
options.D: World Medical Association

explanation: Spot on! The International Council of Nurses sets the global standard definition that highlights both our independent and teamwork roles in healthcare. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is it so hard to listen to breath sounds with a regular stethoscope inside a flying aircraft?

options.A: Flight nurses are not permitted to use stethoscopes
options.B: Air pressure changes destroy the rubber tubing instantly
options.C: Patients stop breathing entirely when the engine starts
options.D: The high level of ambient engine noise masks lung sounds

explanation: Correct! Aircraft engines are very loud. Because the background noise makes auscultation tough, flight nurses rely heavily on monitors and capnography.

question: What is the primary purpose of using supportive devices like pillows and trochanter rolls?

options.A: To prevent the patient from speaking
options.B: To increase patient body temperature
options.C: To maintain correct body alignment
options.D: To speed up intravenous infusion rates

explanation: Supportive devices keep joints in a natural, neutral position to prevent deformities like footdrop and muscle strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h1)

question: What is the primary age threshold that defines early marriage globally?

options.A: Under 21 years
options.B: Under 16 years
options.C: Under 18 years
options.D: Under 15 years

explanation: Global public health and human rights frameworks classify any marriage involving a person under 18 years as an early or child marriage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h1)

question: What is a tracheostomy?

options.A: A tube inserted through the nose into the stomach
options.B: A small incision made in the upper chest wall
options.C: A flexible scope passed down the throat
options.D: A surgical opening made into the trachea

explanation: A tracheostomy involves creating a surgical opening directly into the trachea through the neck. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h1)

question: A patient on tiopronin calls reporting a sudden sore throat, fever, and skin rash. What should you advise?

options.A: Suggest taking an over-the-counter antihistamine and doubling the evening water intake
options.B: Tell the patient this is a normal harmless side effect that will resolve in a few days
options.C: Advise the patient to stop the medication and report to the clinic immediately for lab work
options.D: Recommend waiting until the next scheduled routine appointment next month

explanation: Fever, sore throat, and rash can be warning signs of a serious reaction or blood issue. It's always best to pause the drug and have the medical team check them right away!

question: What is the usual long-term outlook for children who get Acute Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Poor, with guaranteed progression to failure
options.B: Moderate, leading to chronic heart disease
options.C: Excellent, with most making a full recovery
options.D: Unpredictable, with lifelong dialysis needed

explanation: Unlike adults, kids with AGN almost always bounce back completely with the right care and rest. Such a relief to know for young patients and their families!

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Cover the tiny puncture wound tightly with adhesive tape
options.B: Wash the site immediately with soap and running water
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to report it
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow joint

explanation: Immediate washing helps remove and flush out infectious pathogens before they can establish an infection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h6)

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse should do for a patient who has a hazardous liquid chemical spilled on their skin?

options.A: Apply neutralizing acidic or basic ointments
options.B: Remove all contaminated clothing immediately
options.C: Administer an oral antidote medication
options.D: Draw baseline arterial blood gas samples

explanation: Safety first! Stripping away the wet clothing stops the chemical from continuing to soak into the skin or burn the patient.

question: What is the primary characteristic of a malignant neoplasm compared to a benign one?

options.A: It invades nearby tissues and spreads to other parts of the body.
options.B: It stops growing entirely after a few weeks without treatment.
options.C: It only affects older adults and ignores younger populations.
options.D: It stays localized in one spot and never grows very large.

explanation: Malignant neoplasms are cancerous because they can break away, invade surrounding structures, and travel through the blood or lymph system. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h1)

question: A patient has an infected open leg fracture that hasn't healed over the past eight months, despite short courses of oral antibiotics. What type of osteomyelitis is this?

options.A: Aseptic bone infarction
options.B: Transient bone bruising
options.C: Acute hematogenous osteomyelitis
options.D: Chronic osteomyelitis

explanation: When an infection sticks around for many months and fights off standard treatments, it has turned into chronic osteomyelitis.

question: What is the main use of an ultrasonic cleaner in the CSSD?

options.A: Killing bacterial spores using high heat
options.B: Removing microscopic debris using sound waves
options.C: Applying a protective rust-proof coating
options.D: Drying moisture from surgical hinges

explanation: Ultrasonic cleaners use high-frequency sound waves to create tiny scrubbing bubbles that blast hidden dirt out of tiny instrument hinges and joints.

question: While trying to do a manual flush, you feel a lot of resistance on the syringe plunger. What is your next move?

options.A: Push harder on the plunger to force the clot out
options.B: Inject twice as much fluid to clear the blockage
options.C: Pull the catheter halfway out of the urethra
options.D: Stop pushing immediately and report the resistance

explanation: Never force it! Pushing against a blockage can tear the delicate bladder wall or urethra. Stop and let the doctor know.

question: Why do nurses prefer to use a clear, transparent dressing over an IV insertion site?

options.A: It completely stops the patient from feeling any accidental movement pain.
options.B: It allows the nurse to inspect the skin for redness without removing the cover.
options.C: It keeps the cannula warm so the IV fluid flows much faster.
options.D: It permanently seals the vein shut so no blood can ever leak out.

explanation: Spot on! Clear dressings keep outside germs away while letting you quickly check the site for early signs of swelling or redness without peeling anything back.

question: Which activity is generally not safe for someone with unmanaged seizures?

options.A: Swimming alone in deep water
options.B: Reading books in a well-lit room
options.C: Walking outside during the daytime
options.D: Drinking plenty of clean water

explanation: Safety first! If a seizure hits while swimming alone, the risk of drowning is extremely high. Advising against solo swimming is a crucial part of patient education.

question: A client with rheumatoid arthritis wakes up with severe joint stiffness that lasts for nearly two hours. What does this tell you as a nurse?

options.A: It represents normal muscle fatigue from daily exercise
options.B: It indicates active and ongoing systemic inflammation
options.C: It suggests the client is experiencing a sudden bone fracture
options.D: It points to a localized soft tissue injury from a fall

explanation: Morning stiffness that drags on for an hour or more is a major red flag for active inflammation inside the joints. Great nursing assessment catches this early!

question: How is an idiosyncratic drug reaction different from a regular side effect?

options.A: It only happens when a patient takes an overdose of medicine.
options.B: It can be easily predicted by checking standard blood test results.
options.C: It is a mild response that always goes away without any treatment.
options.D: It is completely unpredictable and does not depend on the drug dose.

explanation: Think of an idiosyncratic reaction as a surprise response! Unlike normal side effects that we expect, these happen out of nowhere due to a patient's unique body makeup, not because of a high dose. You've got this!

question: Why is the PTA considered a bridge between the home and the school?

options.A: It collects school fees on behalf of the government
options.B: It sets the national curriculum for basic education
options.C: It controls the promotion and demotion of teachers
options.D: It fosters cooperation and shared responsibility for child welfare

explanation: The association connects family life with school life so both sides can work together toward the child's health and learning goals. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why does a client with untreated diabetes experience frequent urination?

options.A: The kidneys enlarge to remove excess protein from the bloodstream
options.B: Excess glucose pulls water into the urine through osmotic diuresis
options.C: Infections destroy the sphincter muscles that control urine release
options.D: High blood sugar directly irritates the lining of the urinary bladder

explanation: When sugar spills into the urine, it acts like a sponge, drawing extra water along with it and causing high urine output. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h4)

question: A woman who has given birth many times is at 32 weeks pregnant and reports painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Uterine rupture
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Incompetent cervix
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: Painless bleeding in the third trimester is a classic sign of placenta previa, which is more common when past births have caused changes or scarring in the womb.

question: What is the most common minor issue that can happen after a paracentesis?

options.A: Persistent fluid leakage from the site
options.B: Sudden loss of the sense of taste
options.C: Complete failure of both kidneys
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the legs

explanation: Sometimes a little bit of fluid keeps oozing out if the tiny hole takes a little longer to seal shut.

question: Which nursing action shows safe and professional use of the partograph?

options.A: Completing all the missing shifts' entries at the end of the week from memory
options.B: Plotting data accurately in real time and notifying the doctor when lines are crossed
options.C: Waiting until complete uterine rupture occurs before looking at the chart
options.D: Hiding the partograph from the medical team to avoid paperwork scrutiny

explanation: Always chart as you go! Real-time plotting ensures that the moment a warning line is crossed, the whole team can jump into action.

question: How does pursed-lip breathing help a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease?

options.A: It forces extra oxygen directly into the bloodstream through the mouth
options.B: It relaxes the stomach muscles to improve digestion
options.C: It stops the patient from coughing up thick mucus plugs
options.D: It slows down exhalation and keeps airways open longer

explanation: Pursed-lip breathing creates back-pressure in the airways, preventing them from collapsing too early and helping trap less air in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h5)

question: What is the very first priority when handling a suspected child abuse case?

options.A: Reuniting the child with extended family members immediately
options.B: Ensuring the physical safety and medical stabilization of the child
options.C: Conducting a lengthy family therapy session at the bedside
options.D: Waiting for legal court orders before treating physical wounds

explanation: Safety first! Always treat urgent medical needs and get the child away from immediate danger before anything else.

question: Which beverage is generally allowed during the fasting period prior to the test?

options.A: Black coffee
options.B: Fruit juice
options.C: Plain water
options.D: Sweetened tea

explanation: Plain water has no calories or active compounds that stimulate digestion, keeping the fasting state intact while preventing dehydration. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the absolute best way to check if a patient is ready to give their own shots at home?

options.A: Ask a family member to take full responsibility for the task
options.B: Provide a written multiple-choice test on injection theory
options.C: Have the patient perform a return demonstration of the steps
options.D: Ask the patient to read the medication package insert aloud

explanation: Seeing is believing! Having them show you how they do it lets you coach them, build their confidence, and make sure they are doing it safely.

question: Why does an anticholinergic drug need to cross the blood-brain barrier to help with brain disorders?

options.A: To speed up the breakdown of extra dopamine
options.B: To stop the drug from entering the bloodstream
options.C: To reach target receptors located inside the brain
options.D: To block heart receptors right away

explanation: Makes total sense! For a drug to treat a condition in the central nervous system, it has to be able to cross that protective blood-brain barrier to get where it's needed.

question: What is the biggest benefit of different healthcare professionals working together as an interprofessional team?

options.A: It eliminates the need for daily nursing documentation
options.B: It allows each discipline to work completely independently
options.C: It ensures only physicians make final clinical decisions
options.D: It prevents confusion and mixed messages through shared communication

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! When doctors, nurses, and therapists share their observations, it stops conflicting instructions and helps patients recover faster.

question: What should a healthy, newly formed intestinal stoma look like when you check it?

options.A: Pink and moist
options.B: Pale and dry
options.C: Dark purple or black
options.D: Cold and hard

explanation: Great job! A healthy stoma has great blood flow, so it should look pink to red and feel moist. A dark purple or black stoma means trouble with blood supply and is an emergency!

question: You walk into a ward and see that your patient's traction weights are resting on the floor. What is your very next move?

options.A: Lift the weights and ensure they hang freely
options.B: Remove the traction apparatus immediately
options.C: Add more weight to make up for lost time
options.D: Document that the therapy is finished

explanation: Quick thinking! Just lift them up so they hang free again, and traction is instantly restored.

question: Who typically acts as the central coordinator connecting various specialists and the patient in clinical settings?

options.A: The hospital accountant
options.B: The facility security guard
options.C: The pharmaceutical supplier
options.D: The nurse

explanation: Nurses coordinate care pathways, schedule referrals, and bridge communication between patients and the multidisciplinary healthcare team. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h7)

question: When do accidental needle-stick injuries most frequently occur in clinical settings?

options.A: When storing unopened boxes of sterile syringes in the pharmacy
options.B: During the physical assessment of a newly admitted patient
options.C: While washing hands with soap and water before a procedure
options.D: While recapping used needles after giving an injection

explanation: Trying to put the cap back onto a used needle is a leading cause of accidental punctures in nursing practice. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in any hospital?

options.A: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.B: Administering daily multivitamins
options.C: Changing bed linen every morning
options.D: Wearing sterile gloves for all tasks

explanation: Spot on! Good old-fashioned hand hygiene is your number one weapon against hospital-acquired infections.

question: Why do doctors order antibody blood tests like rheumatoid factor when checking joint pain?

options.A: To evaluate how well the kidneys filter waste products
options.B: To measure the exact daily amount of calcium in the bones
options.C: To determine if the client has an active bacterial wound infection
options.D: To check for specific proteins that indicate an autoimmune attack

explanation: Tests like rheumatoid factor look for rogue proteins that show the immune system is mistakenly attacking the body's own healthy joint tissues.

question: What does a nurse do when acting as a facilitator of health education?
